title: evidence subcommand does not handle collect failures and can crash instead of returning exit 2

finding.claim: evidence subcommand does not handle collect failures and can crash instead of returning exit 2
finding.evidence: The new config-driven evidence path calls collect directly with no exception handling, unlike the surrounding file's other CLI entrypoints that convert operational failures into exit code 2. Any runtime error from configured commands/adapters will now propagate and terminate the process.
finding.recommendation: Wrap the call to evidence_mod.collect, and ideally the subsequent file write, in a try/except that reports the error to stderr and returns 2 so the subcommand preserves its documented contract for inconclusive or infrastructure errors.

probe.summary: CLI probe (`probes/closingB_cli_core.py`, evidence section): a config whose `timeout` is the numeric string "10" passes load_config validation and reaches Popen inside collect, raising TypeError — at span head the exception propagated out of `_evidence_main` (a real invocation dies with a traceback and exit 1, not the documented exit 2). Only load_config's ValueError was guarded. FIXED in this workup: _evidence_main now guards collect the same way (reason printed, return 2), with a parent-fail-verified regression test (the test errors with the TypeError on the pre-fix source).
